prompt:
You are about to be evaluated in GameScientist, a benchmark in which AI models play commercial video games from screenshots with ordinary keyboard and mouse input. Before the run starts we would like to interview you. This conversation is separate: nothing written here is shown to you during play.

Model under test: gpt-6-astra.
Game: Don't Starve.
About the game: Don't Starve is a real-time survival and crafting game. A trial starts Wilson in an undeveloped first-day base-game world with DLC disabled and the official Long Day option, retaining a day/dusk/night cycle. This setting measures early continuous survival and ordinary resource, crafting, building and food progress rather than Adventure Mode completion. The exact life limit, charged-time cap, execution mode and rubric are supplied by the Trial and its separate pre-run interview. Surviving time is never pooled across deaths.
Controls:
W/A/S/D move. Space performs a nearby contextual action. F attacks a nearby target. Left click performs the primary action at the pointer. Right click performs the secondary action at the pointer. Pointer hover reveals native action labels, and dragging moves an object to a selected destination. Escape opens or closes menus, Tab toggles the map, Q/E rotate the camera, and Return confirms menu selections. Scroll changes zoom or scrolls the visible interface. These are ordinary input bindings, not a strategy. Number keys 1 through 9 and 0 activate the native action for items in inventory slots 1 through 10. The native mouse-operated crafting bar uses left clicks to toggle category tabs and pointer hover to select entries; clicking an entry or its native button activates it. The separate keyboard-operated crafting panel uses W/S to select a category, A/D to select an entry, and Space to activate the current selection. In that keyboard panel, a mouse click activates the current selection; moving the pointer does not select another entry.
Choose one ordinary keyboard or mouse input using the screenshot. Keyboard inputs are held for 3 seconds. Left click performs the primary action on the visible target; right click performs its secondary action. Pointing without clicking reveals the native hover label. A drag moves a visible object to a visible destination. Mouse targets are selected from the current screenshot. The profile describes controls only and provides no game objectives. The number keys 1 through 9 and 0 activate inventory slots 1 through 10 using the native inventory action for the item in that slot. Hovering an inventory item displays its native action label. The native mouse-operated crafting bar uses left clicks to toggle category tabs and pointer hover to select entries; clicking an entry or its native button activates it. The separate keyboard-operated crafting panel uses W/S to select a category, A/D to select an entry, and Space to activate the current selection. In that keyboard panel, a mouse click activates the current selection; moving the pointer does not select another entry.
Group action: Select one ordinary input. Its key combination, pointer action or scroll is executed as a single action.
  up: Hold W to move up. In the keyboard-operated crafting panel, selects the previous category.
  left: Hold A to move left. In the keyboard-operated crafting panel, selects the previous entry.
  down: Hold S to move down. In the keyboard-operated crafting panel, selects the next category.
  right: Hold D to move right. In the keyboard-operated crafting panel, selects the next entry.
  up_left: Hold W and A to move diagonally up and left.
  up_right: Hold W and D to move diagonally up and right.
  down_left: Hold S and A to move diagonally down and left.
  down_right: Hold S and D to move diagonally down and right.
  context_action: Hold Space to perform an available nearby contextual action. In the keyboard-operated crafting panel, activates the current selection.
  attack: Hold F to attack a nearby target.
  escape: Press Escape to open or close the current menu.
  map: Press Tab to toggle the map.
  confirm: Press Return to confirm the selected menu item.
  rotate_left: Press Q to rotate the camera left.
  rotate_right: Press E to rotate the camera right.
  scroll_up: Scroll one wheel step upward at the current pointer position.
  scroll_down: Scroll one wheel step downward at the current pointer position.
  inventory_slot_1: Press 1 to activate the item in inventory slot 1. The native item action depends on that item.
  inventory_slot_2: Press 2 to activate the item in inventory slot 2. The native item action depends on that item.
  inventory_slot_3: Press 3 to activate the item in inventory slot 3. The native item action depends on that item.
  inventory_slot_4: Press 4 to activate the item in inventory slot 4. The native item action depends on that item.
  inventory_slot_5: Press 5 to activate the item in inventory slot 5. The native item action depends on that item.
  inventory_slot_6: Press 6 to activate the item in inventory slot 6. The native item action depends on that item.
  inventory_slot_7: Press 7 to activate the item in inventory slot 7. The native item action depends on that item.
  inventory_slot_8: Press 8 to activate the item in inventory slot 8. The native item action depends on that item.
  inventory_slot_9: Press 9 to activate the item in inventory slot 9. The native item action depends on that item.
  inventory_slot_10: Press 0 to activate the item in inventory slot 10. The native item action depends on that item.
  click_target: Left-click a visible target to perform its primary mouse action.
  secondary_target: Right-click a visible target to perform its secondary mouse action.
  point_target: Move the pointer to a visible target without clicking.
  drag_target: Drag a visible object to a visible destination.
How you will play: each turn you see one screenshot and choose one action; the game keeps running while you think. The run allows 1 attempt and lasts at most 3 hours of wall-clock time, including your thinking time. If the game ends an attempt and another remains, the game restarts and you keep notes from earlier attempts.

Rare materials, combat drops, and advanced crafting require exploration and extra interactions that compete with basic survival.
answers.likely_failure: Missing a nightfall or letting a torch or fire expire while navigating crafting and inventory. Hunger and damage during spider encounters or an early hound attack are other likely causes of death. Even if I survive five cycles, I will probably miss several materials or advanced recipes.
answers.helpful_mechanics: Long Day provides more daylight for gathering and exploration. Common resources and simple recipes supply many accessible milestones. Fifty points come from continuous survival alone, so securing food, fuel, and shelter has substantial value. Contextual actions simplify gathering, and a science machine unlocks useful equipment and several scoring opportunities. Cooking improves basic foods, while armor reduces combat risk.
answers.harmful_mechanics: The world continues running while I interpret screenshots and choose actions. Three-second keyboard holds make precise movement and combat harder, and crafting interfaces require careful state tracking. Darkness can kill rapidly; hunger, spoilage, equipment durability, and finite fuel create recurring demands. Random resource distribution can delay gold and specialized materials. There is only one attempt, and survival time cannot be pooled across deaths.
